candidates.decision_relevance: The reviews repeatedly cite weak or improving breadth, but available readings are point-in-time proxies with changing membership and incomplete paths. A consistent historical cross-section would help distinguish persistent participation deterioration from endpoint noise and assess whether recovery broadened.
candidates.evidence_reference: W41/W40 reviews: W41 breadth sequences are not supplied; daily outputs report proxy-only breadth with changing membership hashes and note missing weekly paths.
candidates.metric_name: Fixed-universe constituent returns and advancer/decliner breadth
candidates.missing_history_problem: Snapshots cannot establish the timing, persistence, or breadth of participation changes relative to price drawdowns and recoveries.

candidates.decision_relevance: The analyses use short-window spot taker and depth imbalances, but describe them as snapshots that can reverse between captures. An aligned historical sequence would show whether spot participation and liquidity deterioration persisted or merely coincided with price moves.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily outputs on Oct. 17–18 report capture-to-capture reversals in BTC/ETH spot depth and taker imbalances, and explicitly note that short snapshots do not establish durable behavior.
candidates.metric_name: BTC/ETH spot taker-quote and depth-20 imbalance series
candidates.missing_history_problem: Sparse captures do not reveal persistence or ordering of spot-flow and depth changes relative to returns.

candidates.decision_relevance: Open-interest changes are repeatedly described as point-to-point or horizon-inconsistent, and deleveraging is directionally ambiguous. A continuous history aligned with prices and funding would make the observed leverage changes and their sequence inspectable.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily outputs note modest or horizon-dependent open-interest changes, while W36–W37 reviews identify missing positioning paths and uncertainty about whether deleveraging preceded or followed price weakness.
candidates.metric_name: BTC/ETH open interest and funding history
candidates.missing_history_problem: Isolated changes cannot distinguish persistent exposure build or reduction from transient capture differences, nor establish their temporal relation to price moves.

candidates.decision_relevance: ETF evidence is often limited to one recent settled session, while weekly totals can conceal within-week sequencing. A contiguous history of settled flows would clarify whether reported inflows or outflows persisted and how they aligned with price and participation changes.
candidates.evidence_reference: W40/W41 reviews cite weekly totals but say flow timing or direction is insufficiently specified; daily outputs frequently cite only the latest settled row and note missing sessions.
candidates.metric_name: Daily settled BTC and ETH ETF flow series
candidates.missing_history_problem: Single-session rows and aggregate weekly totals do not show the timing or persistence of flows during the reported drawdowns and recoveries.
